blockNote: Player movement integrator (Bank 02, 176798-177195): the per-frame companion actor that turns the player's velocity inputs into a new position.

SPAWN AND ORDER: PlayerCharacterDef spawns it with SpawnAfter. Every SpawnAfter inserts the new actor directly behind its spawner, and slope_ramp_physics is spawned after this actor, so the actor list reads attack_ability_system, player, slope_ramp_physics, this controller. The slope code has therefore already edited playerSpeedEw / playerSpeedNs when this runs in the same frame. CopyActorState sets the hidden bit ($2000) on it, so only its script runs.

STATE: this actor's own $14 / $16 hold the player's position in SUB-PIXELS (4 per pixel, 2 fractional bits). The x4 scaling at the top runs once, when the actor spawns; every later frame resumes after SetEntryHere. The player actor's $0014 / $0016 stay in plain pixels (the write-back stores sub-pixels >> 2).
PER FRAME:

1. HIT-STUN: if the player's $10 has bit $0080 (the iframe counter is running) and iframeCounter is not negative, skip the frame. A positive counter is hit-stun, so this is the check that freezes the player (actor_execution exempts the player from its own freeze); a negative counter (recovery) lets movement continue.

2. LOCK: if playerFlags has EITHER bit $0200 (game over) or $0800 (script / ability lock) set, clear extVelocityX / Y and skip: the script or the traversal code (stairs, vine, ladder, cutscene) owns the position.
3. SYNC: if the player actor's pixel position differs from local >> 2 (a script or COP moved the player), adopt the actor's position x4; the old fraction is lost.

4. VELOCITY, per axis. Speed word (playerSpeedEw / playerSpeedNs) zero: joypad velocity from JoypadToVelocity plus the external velocity; the joypad part is forced to zero while playerFlags has $1000 (on-slope latch) or $2000 (guard / channel stance). Speed nonzero: speed x 4 plus the external velocity, and the $1000 latch is cleared. One speed unit is one pixel per frame; the joypad gives +/-8 sub-pixels (2 px per frame).

5. MOVE: bit $0008 of the player actor's $10 means 'collision-checked movement' (actor_execution uses the same bit for every actor). Set: player_move_main.PlayerMovementTick runs the tile collision with X = THIS actor's slot, positions in the low-RAM words $22 / $26 and velocities in $20 / $24. Clear (the vine, ladder and shimmy states clear it and restore it on exit): the velocity is added to the position with no collision.
6. WRITE-BACK: local position = $22 / $26; the player actor gets position >> 2; bit $0004 (solid contact, set by the tick in this actor's own $10) is copied into the player's $10.

External velocities ($0408 / $040A) are consumed (zeroed) every frame, so a source must write them every frame to keep pushing: av71_wind_effect, btEA_conveyor_controller, combat_collision (push hits), gw82_archer, sg55_viper. scene_lifecycle clears them and both speed words at scene setup.
JoypadToVelocity (end of file) is called only from here.

PlayerMoveController: Entry and per-frame routine. The scaling of $14 / $16 above SetEntryHere runs only when the actor spawns; the code from SetEntryHere down runs every frame (stages in the block note).
JoypadToVelocity: Packs the D-pad into one word: high byte = Y velocity, low byte = X velocity, signed sub-pixels per frame (positive = east / south). Called only from PlayerMoveController.

Reads the pad's high byte ($0657) in 8-bit mode: bit 0 Right, bit 1 Left, bit 2 Down, bit 3 Up. Left wins over Right and Up over Down. Cardinal moves are +/-8 (2.0 px per frame); a diagonal uses +/-6 on each axis (resultant about 2.1 px per frame, so diagonals are slightly faster than cardinals).

blockNote: Pedestal statue of the inventory screen (Bank 00, 53033-53134): shows one collected mystic statue, or removes itself when that statue is not collected yet.

SPAWN: scene $FF (the inventory overlay) lists six copies right after InventoryMenuDef; scene $FD (the reward ceremony) has the same six positions for statue_inventory_reward. Initial flags $3800 (actor-def header byte): $2000 hidden, $1000 and $0800 keep it running in the display-filtered and cutscene-only actor passes (the inventory main loop uses RunActors_CutsceneOnly).

PARAMETER ($0E): InitActorFromSceneData, mode 1 (spawn byte 2 odd): $0E = (byte AND $FF) >> 1. The low nibble is the index into statue_reward_00CE97 (0-5); bit 4 ($0010) marks a top-row pedestal, moved 8 px up. The actor overwrites $0E with $2000 (the OAM attribute word) after reading it.
| Spawn byte | After >> 1 | Index | Bit 4 | Flag | Sprite | Tile (x,y) | Actor X, Y |
Actor X = tile x 16 + 8 (the engine's centring offset for non-player actors) + 8 (NudgePosition); actor Y = tile y 16 + 8, minus 8 for bit 4. Positions are actor coordinates, not screen pixels.

STATE: TestFlagRaw(flag) returns carry set when the flag is set; flag N is bit (N AND 7) of byte $0A00 + N / 8, so $F8-$FD are bits 0-5 of the single byte $0A1F. Flag clear: COP Die, nothing is drawn. Flag set: InventoryStatueSlotClaimed sets the animation index $28 from table byte +1 ($3A-$3F), runs UpdateActorAnimation and clears the hidden bit; every frame after that inventoryTabIndex = 3 (Status tab) hides the statue and any other tab shows it, so the statues sit beside the item grid only.
The table has 4 bytes per entry (flag, sprite, match, one tail byte); this actor reads +0 and +1. The flags are set by statue_inventory_reward (scene $FD), which this actor only displays.

InventoryStatueSlotClaimed: Reached by JMP from the actor entry with X = table byte offset and the actor slot still on the stack (the first PLX restores it). Sets the statue frame, clears the hidden bit and runs the per-frame tab test.

blockNote: Stat-reward pickup actors of a cleared Dark Space room (Bank 00, 57389-57683): e_hp_increase, e_str_increase and e_def_increase.

SPAWN: EnemyStatBonusReward (in StandardEnemyDefeatHandler) runs when the LAST enemy of a scene is defeated (the remaining-enemy counter in orbitAngle is 0). enemy_clear_reward_table[scene] selects the actor: 1 = HP, 2 = STR, 3 or more = DEF, 0 = nothing. The reward is given once per scene: scene flag $0300 + scene (TestFlag_0300) must be clear and RewardActorVFX sets it. Before spawning, EnemyStatBonusReward sets displayModeFlags $0080 (display filter) and spawns the actor with flags $1000; in the display-filtered pass only actors with bit 12 run, so the rest of the world is frozen while the pickup plays.
EACH ACTOR: sprite frame $0C / $0D / $0E of spriteset_enemies (palette 0), CallNear RewardActorVFX, the stat change, a message and Die.

RewardActorVFX: clears bits $4000 / $2000 of its $12; animation $FF for 4 passes while rising (Y movement chain #12: -1 px every second tick), 3 more passes standing still, then StageMove (speed 2) / TickMove flies it to the player (target = player X, player Y - 8). Then it sets the hidden bit, clears the display filter (the world runs again), plays sound $25 on channel 2, sets scene flag $0300 + scene (reward taken) and returns to the CallNear caller with RestoreSavedPtr.

STAT CHANGE: +1 with a signed-overflow check: BVC skips the clamp unless the sum overflows ($7FFF + 1), which cannot happen with these stats, so the clamp value $0255 is never loaded and nothing caps the stats here (the number of cleared rooms does). HP: max HP + 1 and hpToHeal = new max HP - current HP, so the whole missing HP is refilled by UpdateHUD (one HP per 8-frame step with sound $0D). STR and DEF only add 1.
